Pethahiah, at the king's side on behalf of his people, held a post not unlike Nehemiah's own at Susa. God always had someone at that door.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 25–36 — From Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Judah lives in its villages from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom (vv. 25-30), Benjamin from Geba to Lod and Ono (vv. 31-35), and some Levites of Judah are assigned to Benjamin (v. 36).
verseByVerse.theology: Every name on the list is a town God had given their fathers, and nearly every one has a story. The nine in ten were not second-class; they were living on the promise too.

verseByVerse.quote: And as for the villages, with their fields, some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its villages, and in Dibon and its villages, and in Jekabzeel and its villages, and in Jeshua and in Moladah and Beth-pelet, in Hazar-shual, in Beersheba and its villages, in Ziklag, in Meconah and its villages, in En-rimmon, in Zorah, in Jarmuth, Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, and Azekah and its villages. So they encamped from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Kiriath-arba is the old name of Hebron (Josh 14:15), where Abraham bought a grave and David was first crowned. Then Beersheba, where Abraham dug his wells; Ziklag, given to David; Zorah, where Samson was born; Adullam, David's cave; Lachish and Azekah, the last fortresses to hold out against Babylon. Every town is a chapter of their history, and every one was lived in again.

The old measure of the land was from Dan to Beersheba. Now it runs from Beersheba to the edge of Jerusalem, a fraction of what they had once held. And they encamped, the word used of Israel in the wilderness: back in the land, and still living like pilgrims in it.

The Valley of Hinnom is the valley of Topheth, where Judah's kings had burned their children in the fire (Jer 7:31). Its name in the Greek of the Gospels is Gehenna, the word Jesus used for hell. The people lived up to the edge of the place of their worst sin, in a land given back to them, looking for more than that strip of hill country could give. So are we: here we have no lasting city, but we seek the city that is to come (Heb 13:14).

verseByVerse.quote: The people of Benjamin also lived from Geba onward, at Michmash, Aija, Bethel and its villages, Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah, Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim, Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat, Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen. And certain divisions of the Levites in Judah were assigned to Benjamin.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Michmash, where Jonathan climbed the cliff; Bethel, where Jacob saw the ladder; Anathoth, Jeremiah's town; Ramah, Samuel's home. And Nob, the city of the priests, which Saul put to the sword (1 Sam 22:19). The town of a massacre is a town of families again.

On to Lod and Ono, the plain where Sanballat had tried to lure Nehemiah (6:2). And Levites of Judah were assigned to Benjamin, so that no part of the land was left without teachers of the law.

The patriarchs had lived in this land as strangers too: he was looking forward to the city that has foundations, whose designer and builder is God (Heb 11:10, 16). The tenth who moved to Jerusalem and the nine tenths who stayed were all waiting for that city. Christ has built it, and in it the lot is not needed. Every one of his people lives there.

11.theology:
A tithe of the people is given to the holy city, some by lot and some by free offering, and those who offer are blessed; it is the mark of the Messiah's people that they offer themselves freely (Ps 110:3). Those who stayed on their inheritance were no less God's people, living on his promise.

Yet all of them, in the city and the villages, still encamped in a shrunken land. They were waiting for the city whose builder is God (Heb 11:10), the holy city coming down from heaven where God dwells with his people and every one of them lives (Rev 21:2-3).
11.examples:
One family in ten moved to Jerusalem: a tithe of the people.

The volunteers were blessed.

Both of Tamar's twins, Perez and Zerah, had descendants in the city.

Some of the priests were mighty men of valor.

A descendant of Asaph led the praise; a Persian king paid the singers.

From Dan to Beersheba had shrunk to Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.

Nob, where Saul killed the priests, was lived in again.

12.title: Joy Heard Far Away
12.text: <sup>1</sup>These are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,<sup>2</sup>Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,<sup>3</sup>Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,<sup>4</sup>Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,<sup>5</sup>Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,<sup>6</sup>Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,<sup>7</sup>Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua.<sup>8</sup>And the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who with his brothers was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving.<sup>9</sup>And Bakbukiah and Unni and their brothers stood opposite them in the service.<sup>10</sup>And Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim the father of Eliashib, Eliashib the father of Joiada,<sup>11</sup>Joiada the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan the father of Jaddua.<sup>12</sup>And in the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers' houses: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;<sup>13</sup>of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;<sup>14</sup>of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;<sup>15</sup>of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;<sup>16</sup>of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;<sup>17</sup>of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;<sup>18</sup>of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;<sup>19</sup>of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;<sup>20</sup>of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;<sup>21</sup>of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.<sup>22</sup>In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the Levites were recorded as heads of fathers' houses; so too were the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian.<sup>23</sup>As for the sons of Levi, their heads of fathers' houses were written in the Book of the Chronicles until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib.<sup>24</sup>And the chiefs of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brothers who stood opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, according to the commandment of David the man of God, watch by watch.<sup>25</sup>Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers standing guard at the storehouses of the gates.<sup>26</sup>These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra, the priest and scribe.<sup>27</sup>And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with gladness, with thanksgivings and with singing, with cymbals, harps, and lyres.<sup>28</sup>And the sons of the singers gathered together from the district surrounding Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites;<sup>29</sup>also from Beth-gilgal and from the region of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built for themselves villages around Jerusalem.<sup>30</sup>And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates and the wall.<sup>31</sup>Then I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two great choirs that gave thanks. One went to the south on the wall to the Dung Gate.<sup>32</sup>And after them went Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah,<sup>33</sup>and Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,<sup>34</sup>Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,<sup>35</sup>and certain of the priests' sons with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph;<sup>36</sup>and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God. And Ezra the scribe went before them.<sup>37</sup>At the Fountain Gate they went up straight before them by the stairs of the city of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, to the Water Gate on the east.<sup>38</sup>The other choir of those who gave thanks went to the north, and I followed them with half of the people, on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, to the Broad Wall,<sup>39</sup>and above the Gate of Ephraim, and by the Gate of Yeshanah, and by the Fish Gate and the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate; and they came to a halt at the Gate of the Guard.<sup>40</sup>So both choirs of those who gave thanks stood in the house of God, and I and half of the officials with me;<sup>41</sup>and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets;<sup>42</sup>and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. And the singers sang with Jezrahiah as their leader.<sup>43</sup>And they offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy; the women and children also rejoiced. And the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.<sup>44</sup>On that day men were appointed over the storerooms, the contributions, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to gather into them the portions required by the Law for the priests and for the Levites according to the fields of the towns, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who ministered.<sup>45</sup>And they performed the service of their God and the service of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon.<sup>46</sup>For long ago in the days of David and Asaph there were directors of the singers, and there were songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.<sup>47</sup>And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers; and they set apart that which was for the Levites; and the Levites set apart that which was for the sons of Aaron.
12.overview: The chapter opens with the roll of the priests and Levites from the first return to the generation after Nehemiah: six high priests from Jeshua to Jaddua, the heads of the priestly houses (among them of Iddo, Zechariah, almost certainly the prophet), and the Levites who praised antiphonally as David commanded (vv. 1-26). Then the dedication of the wall: Levites and singers gathered from their villages, the people, gates and wall purified (vv. 27-30), and two great choirs of thanksgiving sent along the top of the wall in opposite directions, one led by Ezra, the other followed by Nehemiah, the northern one walking the builders' route of chapter 3 in reverse, until both stand in the house of God (vv. 31-42). God had made them rejoice with great joy, and the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away (v. 43). That day men are appointed over the storerooms, for Judah rejoiced over its priests and Levites (vv. 44-47).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–26 — In the Days of Nehemiah the Governor and of Ezra
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The priests and Levites who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (vv. 1-9); the high priests from Jeshua to Jaddua (vv. 10-11); the heads of the priestly houses in the next generation, among them Zechariah of the house of Iddo (vv. 12-21); and the Levites recorded down to the days of Darius, who praised as David the man of God commanded, watch by watch, in the days of Joiakim and of Nehemiah and Ezra (vv. 22-26).
verseByVerse.theology: Before the celebration, the roll-call of the men who led the worship for three generations. The joy of verse 43 had a history behind it.

verseByVerse.quote: These are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth, Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah, Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah, Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah, Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Twenty-two heads of priestly houses from the first return, ninety years before. (The Ezra here is not the scribe; he came much later.) Among them Abijah (v. 4), the house of John the Baptist's father (Luke 1:5), and Joiarib and Jedaiah (v. 6), whose names head David's list of priestly courses (1 Chr 24:7).

Why put a list here, just before the dedication? Because the wall was not dedicated by a crowd that had appeared from nowhere. It was dedicated by the heirs of families who had kept the worship going through exile and return. The celebration stands on generations of faithfulness nobody had noticed at the time.

verseByVerse.quote: And the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who with his brothers was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving. And Bakbukiah and Unni and their brothers stood opposite them in the service.
verseByVerse.commentary: Two groups of singers facing each other, one answering the other. That is how many psalms were meant to be sung: a line and its reply, for he is good and his steadfast love endures forever. Mattaniah's family kept that thanksgiving going for a century.

verseByVerse.quote: And Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim the father of Eliashib, Eliashib the father of Joiada, Joiada the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan the father of Jaddua.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Six generations of high priests, from the Jeshua who came home with Zerubbabel to Jaddua, three generations after Eliashib, the high priest of Nehemiah's day. The list has been kept up to date by later hands; verse 22 mentions a Darius who came after Artaxerxes.

The third name is the Eliashib who built the Sheep Gate (3:1). Hold the fourth: a son of Joiada became the son-in-law of Sanballat (13:28). The line of the high priests ran straight into the family of the enemy. The priesthood of Aaron needed a better Priest than any it could produce: one holy, innocent, unstained, separated from sinners (Heb 7:26).

verseByVerse.quote: And in the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers' houses: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah; of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan; of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph; of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai; of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam; of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai; of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan; of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi; of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber; of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
verseByVerse.commentary:
For each of the old houses, the man who led it a generation later: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah; of Ezra, Meshullam, and so on down the list.

One line is easy to pass over: of Iddo, Zechariah (v. 16). The prophet Zechariah was the son of Berechiah, son of Iddo (Zech 1:1), and Ezra calls him simply Zechariah the son of Iddo (Ezra 5:1). This is almost certainly the same man: the prophet who urged the people to finish the temple was the head of a priestly house. He had written, Behold, your king is coming to you (Zech 9:9), words the Gospels would quote of Christ riding into Jerusalem (Matt 21:5), and here he sits quietly in a list of priests, between a Helkai and a Meshullam.

And of Abijah, Zichri (v. 17): the house that would one day have Zechariah the father of John the Baptist in it. The rosters of chapter 12 were running on toward the Gospel of Luke.

verseByVerse.quote: In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the Levites were recorded as heads of fathers' houses; so too were the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian. As for the sons of Levi, their heads of fathers' houses were written in the Book of the Chronicles until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib. And the chiefs of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brothers who stood opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, according to the commandment of David the man of God, watch by watch. Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers standing guard at the storehouses of the gates. These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra, the priest and scribe.
verseByVerse.commentary: The man of God was Moses' title, and here it is David's (as at 2 Chr 8:14), because David ordered the worship of the house as Moses had ordered the tabernacle. The pattern of praise, one choir answering another in shifts, watch by watch, was five hundred years old and still being kept.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 27–43 — The Joy of Jerusalem Was Heard Far Away
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: For the dedication the Levites and singers are gathered from their villages, with cymbals, harps and lyres, and the priests purify themselves, the people, the gates and the wall (vv. 27-30). Nehemiah brings the leaders up onto the wall and forms two great choirs: one goes south with Ezra in front (vv. 31-37), the other north with Nehemiah behind it (vv. 38-39), and both come together in the house of God (vv. 40-42). They offer great sacrifices, God makes them rejoice, the women and children too, and the joy of Jerusalem is heard far away (v. 43).
verseByVerse.theology: Tobiah had said a fox would knock the wall down (4:3). On the day of its dedication two choirs walked along the top of it, singing.

verseByVerse.quote: And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with gladness, with thanksgivings and with singing, with cymbals, harps, and lyres. And the sons of the singers gathered together from the district surrounding Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites; also from Beth-gilgal and from the region of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built for themselves villages around Jerusalem. And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates and the wall.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The wall was finished in Elul (6:15). Its dedication is not dated, but it was not done in a hurry. They sent into every village for the Levites, because the dedication of a wall was to be an act of worship, and worship was their work.

The singers had built themselves villages round Jerusalem, at Netophah, Beth-gilgal, Geba and Azmaveth: a ring of singers' families close enough to come in for their turn.

They purified the stones. What is given to God is made clean first, beginning with those who give it, and the wall built by families with swords at their sides was set apart as holy.

verseByVerse.quote: Then I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two great choirs that gave thanks. One went to the south on the wall to the Dung Gate. And after them went Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah, and Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah, and certain of the priests' sons with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph; and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God. And Ezra the scribe went before them.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Remember Tobiah's fox (4:3). Now the governor brings the leaders of the nation up on top of that wall, and hundreds of people, with trumpets and harps and cymbals, walk along it, singing. The fox's weight was the measure of the enemy's contempt. The wall held a choir.

The southern choir goes toward the Dung Gate with half the leaders of Judah, priests with trumpets, and a descendant of Asaph, Zechariah son of Jonathan, with his relatives playing the musical instruments of David the man of God. And Ezra the scribe went before them. The man who had stood on the wooden platform and read the law from dawn to noon leads the procession on the wall. The Word goes first.

Moses had given the trumpets to the priests (Num 10:8) and said they were to be blown on the day of your gladness over the offerings as a reminder of you before your God (Num 10:10). A reminder, a memorial: the word of Nehemiah's constant prayer, remember. The trumpets on the wall asked God to remember his people on the day of their gladness.

verseByVerse.quote: At the Fountain Gate they went up straight before them by the stairs of the city of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, to the Water Gate on the east. The other choir of those who gave thanks went to the north, and I followed them with half of the people, on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, to the Broad Wall, and above the Gate of Ephraim, and by the Gate of Yeshanah, and by the Fish Gate and the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate; and they came to a halt at the Gate of the Guard.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Read the route against chapter 3. Chapter 3 began at the Sheep Gate and ran past the Tower of Hananel, the Fish Gate, the Broad Wall and the Tower of the Ovens (3:1-11), and the northern choir walks the same stretch in reverse. The stones that Eliashib, the men of Jericho, the goldsmiths and Shallum's daughters had laid are walked over by a choir giving thanks. The builders' work sheet has become a hymn route, and the Tower of Hananel, the landmark of Jeremiah's promise (Jer 31:38), hears the singing.

And Nehemiah does not lead this choir. Ezra goes in front of one; Nehemiah walks behind the other. The governor who had driven the whole work follows the singers.

verseByVerse.quote: So both choirs of those who gave thanks stood in the house of God, and I and half of the officials with me; and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets; and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. And the singers sang with Jezrahiah as their leader.
verseByVerse.commentary: Two processions set out in opposite directions round the city and meet at the house of God. Every stretch of the wall has been walked and sung over, and everything converges on the place where God had put his name. The wall was never the point. It was built round a people, and the people were gathered round God.

verseByVerse.quote: And they offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy; the women and children also rejoiced. And the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Count them: rejoiced, made them rejoice, joy, rejoiced, joy. Five times in one verse. And the source is named: God had made them rejoice. The joy was not the natural relief of a project finished. It was given. Nehemiah had told them that the joy of the LORD was their strength (8:10), and here is that joy, poured out.

The women and children also rejoiced. The wives who had raised the outcry about debt (5:1), the children who had been sold for it (5:5), were singing in the city that had been ruins.

Heard far away was written once before. When the temple foundation was laid ninety years earlier, the old men wept while the young shouted for joy, and no one could tell the joyful shout from the weeping, and the sound was heard far away (Ezra 3:13). That day the joy and the grief were mixed. This day, only the joy is heard.

It was still not the last word; the next chapter is a sad one. But it was a sound of what was coming. Behold, I bring you good news of great joy that will be for all the people (Luke 2:10). And when the King came down the Mount of Olives toward this city, the whole multitude of his disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice; told to silence them, he said, if these were silent, the very stones would cry out (Luke 19:37, 40). Sanballat had asked whether they could revive the stones (4:2). The King said the stones themselves would sing.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 44–47 — For Judah Rejoiced over the Priests
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: That day men are put in charge of the storerooms for the contributions, firstfruits and tithes, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and Levites who ministered (v. 44). Priests, singers and gatekeepers serve as David and Solomon commanded (vv. 45-46), and all Israel, in Zerubbabel's days and Nehemiah's, gives the daily portions (v. 47).
verseByVerse.theology: The joy was turned into provision the same day. It is the right order, and the next chapter shows how quickly the provision lapsed when the leader was away.

verseByVerse.quote: On that day men were appointed over the storerooms, the contributions, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to gather into them the portions required by the Law for the priests and for the Levites according to the fields of the towns, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who ministered. And they performed the service of their God and the service of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon. For long ago in the days of David and Asaph there were directors of the singers, and there were songs of praise and thanksgiving to God. And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers; and they set apart that which was for the Levites; and the Levites set apart that which was for the sons of Aaron.
verseByVerse.commentary:
On the same day as the singing, Nehemiah appoints storekeepers. That is not a fall from joy into bookkeeping but joy doing what joy does: people who are glad of those who serve them want to see them fed. The covenant promises of 10:35-39 were being put into practice.

It is a summary of the best years, and the next chapter shows how thin it could wear: when Nehemiah came back from Susa, the portions had stopped and the Levites had gone home to their fields (13:10). Joy that is not guarded does not keep. But the sound of verse 43 had been real, and God, who made them rejoice, has promised a city where the joy is never interrupted and the singers never go hungry: they shall hunger no more, neither thirst anymore (Rev 7:16).

12.theology:
The book that began with a man weeping over a burned city (1:4) reaches a city whose joy is heard far away, and the joy is God's gift: God had made them rejoice. The wall was built round a people, and the people were gathered round God; the two choirs end in his house.

The joy is a foretaste. The prophet-priest Zechariah, named in this roll, had promised a King coming to Jerusalem (Zech 9:9); when he came, his disciples rejoiced with a loud voice, and he said the stones would cry out if they were silent (Luke 19:37-40). The last city's joy will not be interrupted (Rev 7:16-17).
12.examples:
The prophet Zechariah appears as one line in a list of priests.

The high priest's grandson married Sanballat's daughter.

They purified the wall itself.

Tobiah said a fox would break it down; two choirs walked on top of it.

The northern choir walked the builders' list of chapter 3 backwards.

Ezra went in front; Nehemiah walked behind.

Five words of joy in one verse, and the women and children singing.

They appointed storekeepers on the day of the celebration.

13.title: Remember Me, O My God
13.text: <sup>1</sup>On that day they read from the Book of Moses in the hearing of the people. And in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God,<sup>2</sup>for they did not meet the people of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them—yet our God turned the curse into a blessing.<sup>3</sup>As soon as the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all those of foreign descent.<sup>4</sup>Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our God, and who was related to Tobiah,<sup>5</sup>prepared for Tobiah a large chamber where they had previously put the grain offering, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, wine, and oil, which were given by commandment to the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests.<sup>6</sup>While this was taking place, I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king. And after some time I asked leave of the king<sup>7</sup>and came to Jerusalem, and I then discovered the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, preparing for him a chamber in the courts of the house of God.<sup>8</sup>And I was very angry, and I threw all the household furniture of Tobiah out of the chamber.<sup>9</sup>Then I gave orders, and they cleansed the chambers, and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.<sup>10</sup>I also found out that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, so that the Levites and the singers, who did the work, had fled each to his field.<sup>11</sup>So I confronted the officials and said, "Why is the house of God forsaken?" And I gathered them together and set them in their stations.<sup>12</sup>Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses.<sup>13</sup>And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, and as their assistant Hanan the son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, for they were considered reliable, and their duty was to distribute to their brothers.<sup>14</sup>Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and do not wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for his service.<sup>15</sup>In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the Sabbath, and bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads, which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And I warned them on the day when they sold food.<sup>16</sup>Tyrians also, who lived in the city, brought in fish and all kinds of goods and sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah, in Jerusalem itself!<sup>17</sup>Then I confronted the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day?<sup>18</sup>Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this disaster on us and on this city? Now you are bringing more wrath on Israel by profaning the Sabbath."<sup>19</sup>As soon as it began to grow dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut and gave orders that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. And I stationed some of my servants at the gates, that no load might be brought in on the Sabbath day.<sup>20</sup>Then the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice.<sup>21</sup>But I warned them and said to them, "Why do you lodge outside the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands on you." From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath.<sup>22</sup>Then I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember this also in my favor, O my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your steadfast love.<sup>23</sup>In those days also I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.<sup>24</sup>And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and they could not speak the language of Judah, but only the language of each people.<sup>25</sup>And I confronted them and cursed them and beat some of them and pulled out their hair. And I made them take an oath in the name of God, saying, "You shall not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.<sup>26</sup>Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless, foreign women made even him to sin.<sup>27</sup>Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil and act treacherously against our God by marrying foreign women?"<sup>28</sup>And one of the sons of Jehoiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I chased him from me.<sup>29</sup>Remember them, O my God, because they have desecrated the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.<sup>30</sup>Thus I cleansed them from everything foreign, and I established the duties of the priests and Levites, each in his work;<sup>31</sup>and I provided for the wood offering at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.
13.overview: The law is read against Ammon and Moab (vv. 1-3), while Eliashib the priest has given Tobiah the Ammonite the Levites' storeroom during Nehemiah's absence at the Persian court (vv. 4-6). Returning, Nehemiah clears the rooms (vv. 7-9), asks Why is the house of God forsaken? and restores the Levites (vv. 10-14), shuts the gates against Sabbath trade (vv. 15-22), confronts the foreign marriages and drives away Sanballat's son-in-law (vv. 23-29), and orders the priesthood, ending with a prayer: Remember me, O my God, for good (vv. 30-31).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–9 — In the Courts of the House of God
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The law excluding Ammon and Moab, who hired Balaam to curse Israel, is read and obeyed, and the people separate those of foreign descent (vv. 1-3). But while Nehemiah was at the Persian court, Eliashib the priest had given Tobiah the Ammonite the tithe storeroom (vv. 4-6), and Nehemiah returns, very angry, to clear and cleanse it (vv. 7-9).
verseByVerse.theology: What the wall had kept out while Nehemiah was there, the priest's family had let in through a side door.

verseByVerse.quote: On that day they read from the Book of Moses in the hearing of the people. And in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God, for they did not meet the people of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them—yet our God turned the curse into a blessing. As soon as the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all those of foreign descent.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The law is still being read, as at the Water Gate, and still obeyed. The passage is Deuteronomy 23:3-5: Ammon and Moab had refused a thirsty people bread and water in the wilderness and hired a prophet to curse them.

Two things keep this from being a verdict on blood. The first is Ruth, a Moabite and David's great-grandmother (Ruth 4:17), who said your people shall be my people, and your God my God (Ruth 1:16) and came, as Boaz said, under whose wings you have come to take refuge (Ruth 2:12). The law closed the door to Moab the nation, never to a Moabitess who came to the LORD. The second is the last line: our God turned the curse into a blessing. That is what he does. Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us ... so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles (Gal 3:13-14). The cross has opened the door to every Ammonite and Moabite who comes.

verseByVerse.quote: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our God, and who was related to Tobiah, prepared for Tobiah a large chamber where they had previously put the grain offering, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, wine, and oil, which were given by commandment to the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Now before this. The law excluding Ammonites has just been read, and an Ammonite is already living in the temple. Tobiah, who had mocked the wall (4:3), plotted against it (4:7-8), hired a prophet to frighten Nehemiah (6:12) and written him threatening letters (6:19), had been given a room in the house of God by the man in charge of those rooms, his relative.

And it was the storeroom, for the tithes the covenant had promised (10:37-39). The Levites' food had been moved out to make room for the enemy's furniture. Family loyalty had done what open hostility never could.

verseByVerse.quote: While this was taking place, I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king. And after some time I asked leave of the king and came to Jerusalem, and I then discovered the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, preparing for him a chamber in the courts of the house of God. And I was very angry, and I threw all the household furniture of Tobiah out of the chamber. Then I gave orders, and they cleansed the chambers, and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Twelve years after he arrived (5:14), Nehemiah had gone back to the king, as he had promised (2:6). How long he was away we are not told, but it was long enough for this.

Picture the governor of Judah carrying an Ammonite's household goods out of a temple storeroom, then having the chambers cleansed and the vessels and offerings brought back in.

Some four and a half centuries later another man found the temple courts full of trade and drove them out, and his disciples remembered that it was written, Zeal for your house will consume me (John 2:15-17). Nehemiah cleared one room for a season. Christ's zeal for his Father's house consumed him, and his own body, he said, was the temple to be raised in three days (John 2:19-21).

Artaxerxes is called “king of Babylon” because Persian kings took over the titles of the empire they had conquered (cf. Ezra 6:22, “king of Assyria”).
verseByVerse.note: Nehemiah returned to the king in about 433 BC (the thirty-second year) and later came back to Jerusalem.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 10–14 — Why Is the House of God Forsaken?
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Levites, unpaid, have gone home to their fields (v. 10). Nehemiah confronts the officials, restores the Levites and the tithes, appoints reliable treasurers (vv. 11-13), and asks God not to wipe out his good deeds (v. 14).
verseByVerse.theology: The people's promise to care for God's house had lasted only while someone was watching.

verseByVerse.quote: I also found out that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, so that the Levites and the singers, who did the work, had fled each to his field. So I confronted the officials and said, "Why is the house of God forsaken?" And I gathered them together and set them in their stations. Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses. And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, and as their assistant Hanan the son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, for they were considered reliable, and their duty was to distribute to their brothers.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The tithes had stopped, so the men who led the worship had gone back to their farms to feed their families. The singers of chapter 12, whose joy was heard far away, were out in the fields.

Forsaken is the verb of their oath, We will not neglect the house of our God (10:39), and of their great prayer, which confessed that God did not forsake them (9:17, 19). God had not forsaken his people through centuries of rebellion; they forsook his house as soon as their governor was out of sight.

Nehemiah does not only rebuke: he sets the Levites back in their stations, and the tithes come in. His treasurers were considered reliable, in Hebrew faithful, the word used of Abraham's heart (9:8). Money for God's work is to be handled by men who can be trusted: it is required of stewards that they be found faithful (1 Cor 4:2).

verseByVerse.quote: Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and do not wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for his service.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Wipe out recalls his prayer in chapter 4: let not their sin be blotted out from your sight (4:5). There he asked God not to blot out their sins; here, not to blot out his good deeds. He is not claiming to have earned heaven, but asking that service the people had so quickly undone would not be lost from God's record.

Every believer who has watched years of work unravel knows this prayer, and the gospel answers it beyond Nehemiah's hope: God blots out, not our good deeds, but our sins. I, I am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins (Isa 43:25). The record of debt against us is cancelled, nailing it to the cross (Col 2:14), and of the one who belongs to Christ he says, I will never blot his name out of the book of life (Rev 3:5).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 15–22 — To Keep the Sabbath Day Holy
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Sabbath trade has come back into Jerusalem (vv. 15-16). Nehemiah reminds the nobles why the city burned (vv. 17-18), shuts the gates and sends the merchants away (vv. 19-21), sets Levites at the gates, and asks to be spared by God's steadfast love (v. 22).
verseByVerse.theology: The governor who asks to be remembered asks, in the same breath, to be spared.

verseByVerse.quote: In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the Sabbath, and bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads, which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And I warned them on the day when they sold food. Tyrians also, who lived in the city, brought in fish and all kinds of goods and sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah, in Jerusalem itself! Then I confronted the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day? Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this disaster on us and on this city? Now you are bringing more wrath on Israel by profaning the Sabbath."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Nehemiah's exclamation is in the text: in Jerusalem itself! The covenant had said, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath (10:31). The fish stalls were open.

He is quoting history, and behind it a prophet. Jeremiah had stood at these gates and said, do not bear a burden on the Sabbath day or bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem, and warned, I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem (Jer 17:21, 27). They did, and the gates burned: the news that broke Nehemiah's heart in Susa (1:3). Little more than a decade after the new gates were hung, loaded donkeys were walking through them on the Sabbath.

Nehemiah enforced the Sabbath as governor of a people under the law of Moses, where the day was the sign of the covenant and breaking it was a crime (Exod 31:13-14).

Does the Sabbath bind Christians today? The New Testament calls Sabbaths a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ (Col 2:16–17). The rest the day pictured is found in him: Come to me ... and I will give you rest (Matt 11:28); there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God (Heb 4:9–10). So this commentary holds that the Sabbath is fulfilled in Christ, and that the Lord’s Day, the day of his resurrection, is a gift: Christians gladly set Sunday apart for worship, fellowship and rest, out of joy and wisdom, not as a binding law with rules about work, and no one may bind another’s conscience about days (Rom 14:5). Many godly brothers, with the Westminster Confession of Faith and the 1689 London Baptist Confession, hold that the Lord’s Day is the Christian Sabbath, binding by the fourth commandment, and they keep it with a seriousness every Christian can admire; Seventh-day Adventists hold that Saturday still binds. Faithful Christians differ here, and they can differ as brothers.

So a Christian who must work or shop on a Sunday is not breaking God’s law. But Nehemiah’s grief still teaches: a people who let trade swallow every day of the week soon have no time left for God, and a Lord’s Day guarded for worship and rest is a gift from the One who has given us rest, not a burden.

verseByVerse.quote: As soon as it began to grow dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut and gave orders that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. And I stationed some of my servants at the gates, that no load might be brought in on the Sabbath day. Then the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice. But I warned them and said to them, "Why do you lodge outside the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands on you." From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath. Then I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember this also in my favor, O my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your steadfast love.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The doors he had hung (7:1) to keep out Sanballat are now shut to keep the Sabbath: the wall has become a servant of holiness. When the merchants camped outside it, waiting, he threatened them, and they stopped coming. Then he replaced his own servants at the gates with purified Levites, so that the guarding of the day was itself an act of worship.

Here is the key to all Nehemiah's remember me prayers. In the sentence in which he asks God to remember his service, he asks to be spared, and grounds it in God's hesed, his steadfast love. The man who kept the Sabbath knew he still needed mercy. So do we: none of us has kept God's day or his law perfectly, but Christ obeyed perfectly in our place, and his obedience is counted as ours (Rom 5:19). A Christian can pray both halves of Nehemiah's sentence: Lord, remember what I have done for you; and Lord, spare me, not because of it, but because of your love.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 23–31 — Remember Me, O My God, for Good
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Jews have married women of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab (vv. 23-24). Nehemiah confronts them with Solomon's example (vv. 25-27), drives away Sanballat's son-in-law from the high priest's family (vv. 28-29), orders the priesthood, and prays to be remembered for good (vv. 30-31).
verseByVerse.theology: The book ends with a prayer, not a triumph. The man who rebuilt the wall could not rebuild a heart, and he knew it, so his last words ask God to remember him, the prayer Jesus answered for a dying thief (Luke 23:43; see on v. 31).

verseByVerse.quote: In those days also I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and they could not speak the language of Judah, but only the language of each people. And I confronted them and cursed them and beat some of them and pulled out their hair. And I made them take an oath in the name of God, saying, "You shall not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The children could not speak the language of Judah. At the Water Gate the law was read so that the people understood the reading (8:8); these children could not have understood a word of it, nor followed the psalms or the prayers. The marriages were producing a generation shut out of God's Word by the language of their homes. It is a warning to every Christian home: children learn the language of what is loved at the table.

The record is honest about Nehemiah's methods. Ezra, faced with the same sin, pulled out his own hair (Ezra 9:3); Nehemiah pulled out theirs. Christ's servant, by contrast, must not be quarrelsome but kind to everyone ... correcting his opponents with gentleness (2 Tim 2:24-25).

Is this about race? No: the danger was that their children could not speak the language of Judah and so could not hear the law, and that foreign wives drew men to their gods (v. 26). Ruth the Moabite was welcomed by faith. The Christian rule is marriage only in the Lord (1 Cor 7:39). Nehemiah’s violence was the act of a governor under Israel’s law, not a pattern for church leaders. Nor does Nehemiah, unlike Ezra (Ezra 10), break up these marriages: his oath concerns marriages still to come, and for a Christian already married to an unbeliever Paul’s word stands, he should not divorce her (1 Cor 7:12).

verseByVerse.quote: Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless, foreign women made even him to sin. Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil and act treacherously against our God by marrying foreign women?"
verseByVerse.commentary:
Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? He argues from the best example Israel had. Beloved by his God: at his birth God had named him Jedidiah, beloved of the LORD (2 Sam 12:25). Wiser than any man, blessed beyond any king, yet his wives had him build shrines for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, on the mountain east of Jerusalem, and for Molech the abomination of the Ammonites (1 Kgs 11:7): Moab and Ammon, the very peoples of verse 23. If the wisest king in Israel's history was drawn away, nobody in Jerusalem was safe.

Act treacherously echoes Nehemiah's first prayer: If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you (1:8). The sin that had once ended in exile was being committed again inside the rebuilt wall.

verseByVerse.quote: And one of the sons of Jehoiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I chased him from me. Remember them, O my God, because they have desecrated the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Sanballat, who had jeered at the Jews and plotted to kill their governor, had married his daughter into the high priest's own family. The law required the high priest to marry a virgin of his own people (Lev 21:14), and this was a grandson who might one day hold that office. The enemy who could not get over the wall had married into the priesthood.

This one is remember them, not remember me. Malachi, who seems to have preached at about this time, said the same to the priests: You have corrupted the covenant of Levi, and Judah ... has married the daughter of a foreign god (Mal 2:8, 11). The priesthood of Aaron was failing from the top. It needed a Priest whose covenant could not be corrupted, and whose bride would be made clean by his own blood.

verseByVerse.quote: Thus I cleansed them from everything foreign, and I established the duties of the priests and Levites, each in his work; and I provided for the wood offering at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.
verseByVerse.commentary:
His summary of a life's work ends on firewood and firstfruits: the wood offering arranged by lot (10:34), so that the fire on the altar would never go out, and the first of the harvest brought to God. Not the wall, not the fifty-two days, not the king's favour. He had learned what matters.

For good is the word of chapter 2, where the good hand of God was on him and the people strengthened their hands for the good work (2:8, 18). The reforms he had made once he had to make again, so he handed the account to God.

Four and a half centuries later, outside the walls of this same city, a dying thief prayed almost the same prayer: Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom. He was answered at once: Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise (Luke 23:42-43). The King on that cross remembers everyone who asks, and brings them where the wall never needs rebuilding and nothing unclean gets in. I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more (Heb 8:12).

13.theology:
Every promise of chapter 10 (marriages, Sabbath, tithes, the house of God) is found broken. The law was good and the covenant sincere, but the heart was unchanged. Nehemiah could reform a city, but not write the law on a heart. That needs the new covenant (Jer 31:33), in which God puts his Spirit within his people and causes them to walk in his ways (Ezek 36:27), and says, I will remember their sins no more (Heb 8:12).

His three prayers to be remembered (vv. 14, 22, 31) rest on God's steadfast love, not his record (v. 22), and their answer is the crucified King who remembered a dying thief.
13.examples:
The chapter is a catalogue of slippage. The law against Ammonites was read while an Ammonite was living in the temple, in a storeroom emptied of the Levites' food to make room for his furniture. The singers whose joy had been heard far away were back in their fields, fish was sold on the Sabbath in Jerusalem itself, and Sanballat's daughter had married into the high priest's family.

Against all that, Nehemiah's last recorded acts were humble ones, providing firewood and firstfruits, and his last words were a prayer: Remember me, O my God, for good.
